baselines.linker: object-centric 3 mm trajectory with 120/5 active and mimic PD
baselines.xhand: official reference trajectory with 120/5 finger PD
baselines.wuji: v1 no-temporal trajectory with 120/5 finger PD

fixed_physics.note: the final hold and success duration remain 0.5 s for every replay frequency

candidates.reason: tests whether faster execution preserves the expert motion while reducing time available for gravity-driven slip
current common baseline; 70 frames take 3.5 s before the fixed 0.5 s hold
a modest slowdown that gives the PD controller 33 percent more physical settling time per command interval
a common low-rate demonstration playback boundary; doubles tracking time relative to 20 Hz without using the reference script's extreme 1 Hz setting

method_boundary.what_changes: only the interpolation duration between consecutive commands
method_boundary.what_does_not_change: all 70 command values, object initialization, PD gains, friction, success height, sustain duration and final hold duration
method_boundary.interpretation: controller/execution ablation rather than a new geometric retargeting objective
method_boundary.no_slower_search: below 10 Hz would make each 70-frame replay longer than 7 s and risks improving the benchmark mainly through excessive settling rather than better retargeting

selection_rule: for each hand, compare 30/15/10 Hz with its existing 20 Hz baseline on identical A keys; only the single rate with higher success and positive paired net gain may enter the already-frozen E set; ties choose the rate closest to 20 Hz; E must again have positive net gain before replacing 20 Hz

linker.decision: reject all; 30 Hz only ties success with two regressions and much lower final lift

xhand.decision: reject all; slowdown monotonically reduces success and lift, while 30 Hz also loses one net success

wuji.decision: reject all; 20 Hz is the best tested global replay frequency

overall_decision: no replay-frequency candidate enters E; retain 20 Hz for all three hands
